summary: Space Relics is an educational digital museum that explores NASA equipment left on the Moon and Mars. It presents the stories of historic rovers, landers, and scientific instruments through images, timelines, and simple explanations. The project explains why these machines were sent, what scientific discoveries they helped make, and what happened after their missions. Our goal is to make space exploration interesting and understandable for school students. The project uses NASA mission information and relevant NASA data resources to support learning about space technology and exploration.
details:
Our project, "Space Relics", is an interactive digital storytelling platform that explores abandoned equipment, spacecraft parts, and mission-related objects on the Moon and Mars.

The main aim is to explain the history and importance of these objects through simple stories, images, and information. Users can explore different space missions and learn why equipment was left behind, what purpose it served, and how it contributes to space exploration history.

The platform is planned to include a visual gallery, mission information, object descriptions, and an interactive map showing selected locations. It will use NASA images and publicly available mission data as its main information sources.

The project is intended to be developed as a web-based presentation using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Its main benefit is to make space exploration history easier to understand and more interesting for students and the public.

Our idea combines science, technology, and storytelling to preserve the history of human exploration beyond Earth.
